coverage.assessment: Three cues are cut: 'what to do next' (leaving Sir James's shrug unprompted), 'Letters will always be forwarded' (leaving 'You are going away?' less motivated) and Julius's 'supposing he's dead' premise for 'What about marriage?'.

The move from hotel to car is unmarked but recoverable through 'Julius was bending over the car'. The nurse is introduced before the advertising advice. The note is left in Julius's empty sitting-room. The page-boy delivers the telegram at her door.

Attribution stays clear. Turn-taking in the proposal is compressed: 'more dollars', the hysterical-laugh refusal and 'I call your bluff' are cut, as is Tuppence's broken-off 'I thought----' at the leave-taking.
Monday and last Wednesday, 'after' Julius's fall, the night train, 'probably with other relations', the qualified advice to advertise and the Scotland departure are all intact.
Nothing is disclosed prematurely. The cut of 'clinging to her belief that Julius also had withheld something' and of Julius's sideways glance weakens the shared-suspicion texture during the drive.
Self-mockery and V3 and V4 survive. The cut of her struggle for self-control and the five-minute nose-blowing recovery collapses the comic-emotional timing into an abrupt 'That's that'.
The contrast between Sir James's spoken hope and his silent head shake is lost. So is the 'jumped on sentiment' setup that gives 'false to your principles' its point.
All four dependencies are intact against the partner revisions (026, 019, 028).

strengths: Hall's dating ('To-day is Monday... last Wednesday') and the 'Before, or after?' exchange are preserved exactly, with Julius's 'Nurse Edith' recognition and V1.
Sir James's low-voiced holiday line and the 'Never tell all you know' hint keep his smooth legal cadence and stay neutral.
The safe recollection ('the pause before his reply, “Nothing.”') and 'Nothing particular' retain the reciprocal reticence.
The closing run ('Impossible... Monstrous--yet it explained everything', the note, the telegram hook) is intact and reveals nothing prematurely.
summary: The revision keeps every planned clue and continuity point. These include Monday and last Wednesday, Sir James's head shake seen by Julius, the cryptic hint, Julius's 'Nothing', the unnamed 'impossible' idea, the undisclosed note and the telegram as Tuppence perceives it. Neither suspect is exposed. Compared with the first draft, however, the revision cuts several connective beats. Sir James's spoken 'go on hoping', which his head shake contradicts, is gone. So is the 'letters forwarded' cue for 'You are going away?' Tuppence's stated reason for withholding the hint from Julius is cut, along with the 'supposing he's dead' and day-dreaming frame of the proposal. At the mirror, her struggle and five-minute recovery are also gone. None of these is a blocker, but they thin causality, irony and Tuppence's voice.
